designPlan.artDirection: A premium Roblox main menu built around a luminous cyan-to-cobalt glossy material system with thick navy edge framing, restrained warm gold highlights, and elegant ornamental corner accents. The composition centers on a commanding vertical action stack beneath a framed title plate carrying live AURORA text, while settings and credits appear as controlled overlay panels that feel part of the same skin family rather than separate systems. Decorative artwork stays peripheral and low-contrast so the native background breathes and the interface remains readable. All major skins and icons are planned as Gemini-generated matching assets: button skins, panel shells, title plate, slider track and handle, toggle on/off pieces, and play/settings/credits/close icon family. Text remains fully live, crisp, and high-contrast over glossy surfaces.

composition.focalPoint: The unmistakable focal point is the large central Play button directly under the AURORA title plate, with Settings and Credits grouped beneath as primary companion actions. Modal panels open above the same center axis so interaction flow remains concentrated and no empty disconnected center emerges.
secondaryRegions: top_title_plate frames the live AURORA title and anchors the screen identity.
settings_modal overlays the center with a medium panel containing music and volume controls plus close.
credits_modal overlays the center with a smaller compact panel and close.
background_frame provides restrained ornamental corners and subtle ambient framing without competing with the action stack.
composition.alignmentSystem: Strict centered vertical axis for title and action hierarchy, with internal left-right alignment inside modals for readable settings rows. Main actions use a unified vertical dock with equal widths for secondary peers and a larger Play CTA above them. Decorative corners mirror diagonally and never break the centered composition. Panels align to the same central axis as the main menu to preserve hierarchy across desktop and mobile.

visualSystem.colorRationale: Cyan and cobalt carry the rich glossy fantasy-tech identity, navy provides the thick structural edges and shadow depth, and warm gold is reserved for trims, highlights, and selected emphasis so the screen feels premium without becoming multicolored noise. Text is near-white with a softer secondary blue-gray for supporting labels, preserving readability over saturated artwork.
visualSystem.outlineStyle: Thick navy outer framing with a thinner inner cyan-gold highlight edge on hero controls and panels. Decorative pieces use the same navy contour language so generated assets form one kit. Text itself stays clean with minimal or no stroke except subtle shadow for contrast.
visualSystem.shadowStyle: Deep cool shadow under primary surfaces with medium blur and short offset, plus restrained glossy top highlight baked into artwork. Primary CTA gets the strongest shadow layer; companion action buttons and panels use slightly shallower depth to preserve hierarchy.

display.treatment: Used only for the live AURORA title, centered, slightly tracked, bright near-white with subtle navy drop shadow and no heavy outline.

heading.treatment: Panel headings and prominent labels, crisp and readable over glossy surfaces with mild shadow only.

button.treatment: High-contrast live button text centered with icon pairing, no baked lettering, slight shadow for readability against bright cyan-cobalt skins.

body.treatment: Used for panel body text and settings labels with consistent line height and strong contrast.

caption.treatment: Used for short helper text and credits detail with softer secondary text color.

numeric.treatment: Reserved for live slider value display if shown, tabular clarity without decorative treatment.

badge.treatment: Not emphasized on this screen, but kept consistent for any tiny fixed chip-like labels within control artwork if needed.

motionSystem.hover: Desktop hover uses a coherent premium response: buttons lift slightly, gloss intensifies, inner gold edge catches light, and shadows deepen. Slider hover gently enlarges the handle; toggle hover slightly brightens the track. Panels themselves remain stable to avoid visual noise.
motionSystem.press: Press feedback is quick and tactile: buttons compress 3 to 4 percent with a short inset shadow change, toggle thumb depresses before switching, and slider handle compresses subtly at drag start. Motion stays controlled and polished rather than bouncy.
motionSystem.entrance: On menu reveal, title plate and action stack fade and rise in with stagger under 220ms total impression, while decorative corners softly fade without travel. Modals fade and scale in from 97 to 100 percent so they feel attached to the UI shell.
motionSystem.release: Release returns controls smoothly to their resting scale with shadow normalization and gloss settling. Closing modals fades them out and slightly scales to 98 percent before hiding.
motionSystem.reducedMotion: When reduced motion is preferred, remove lift and travel; keep only small opacity and brightness changes plus immediate state transitions for toggle and slider.
motionSystem.touchBehavior: Touch devices use Activated and drag interactions only, never synthetic hover. Press feedback occurs on touch-down with a slightly longer visible state so taps feel responsive on mobile.

audioSystem.touchBehavior: No UI sounds on touch because audio was not requested.
audioSystem.fallbackBehavior: If a future implementation adds sounds, unresolved audio must be reported and the interface should remain silent rather than fabricating assets.

responsiveStrategy.desktop: View builds _NexusDesktop containing the centered title plate, central action stack, and hidden modal overlays. Desktop preserves ornamental corners at moderate visibility and uses broader modal widths with left-aligned internal content. Buttons rely on hover plus press states, and the Play button remains the clear visual anchor while Settings and Credits remain primary companion actions.
responsiveStrategy.mobile: View also builds _NexusMobile with the same semantic node names beneath the mobile group. Runtime selects it when min(viewport.X, viewport.Y)<600. Mobile reflows the title plate narrower, keeps the primary stack centered but lower for thumb comfort, enlarges touch targets to 48-56px minimum, reduces decorative intensity, and widens modals relative to screen width. No desktop-only hover behavior is synthesized on touch.
responsiveStrategy.tablet: Tablet uses the mobile runtime group when under the runtime threshold logic only if min dimension is below 600; otherwise desktop group remains appropriate. Plan visual scaling so tablet landscape reads like a roomy desktop composition, while portrait tablet still has sufficient modal width and touch target sizing through constraints and UIScale adjustments.

implementationNotes: Create both _NexusDesktop and _NexusMobile Frame groups at View.build() return, each containing matching semantic nodeName counterparts for all visible components; desktop visible initially.
Use local helper functions inside View for repeated construction of glossy button shells, title plate framing, panel shells, labels, and ornamental image wrappers.
Use a shared ButtonEffects module for all hover/press interactions; do not duplicate ad hoc tween logic per button.
Implement actual controller-backed panel state with one active modal at a time: opening Settings hides Credits, opening Credits hides Settings, close buttons hide only their respective panel.
Play interaction must close the menu root and then fire a clearly named local hook such as OnPlayRequested or equivalent local bindable callback; do not invent remote networking.
Provide nonvisual controller nodes named PanelStateController and OnPlayRequestedHook to make the intended runtime wiring explicit for verification.
Keep main screen free of unrequested systems: no shop, no rewards, no currency, no progression, no tabs beyond requested actions, no inventory, no ranks.
Modal backdrops may dim the hero stack with a semi-transparent navy overlay, but the overlay should be part of modal handling rather than a new navigation system.
For generated artwork, keep labels as live TextLabel/TextButton text layered above image skins; never bake Play, Settings, Credits, Close, or AURORA into images.
Use distinct child artwork pieces for slider track and handle, and for toggle on/off states, under the existing slider and toggle parent controls so the controller can update state cleanly.
Use UIAspectRatioConstraint on ornamental and artwork pieces that must preserve fixed proportions, especially title plate ends, corner details, toggle art, and slider handle.
Use UITextSizeConstraint on all live text-bearing controls to preserve readability across desktop, tablet, and phone portrait widths.

If credits content is not specified beyond having a small panel, keep it concise and generic, such as a short heading and a brief live text block, without inventing extra systems or long scrollable lists.
Panels should start hidden and be opened and closed by the actual controller, not by View-only static visibility assumptions.
Because audio was not requested, the UI must remain silent rather than attaching placeholder sound assets.
The background should be native Roblox UI layering with restrained gradients and bloom-like panels, not a full illustrated splash that overpowers the controls.

iconSystem.styleDescription: Distinct matching Gemini-generated icon family for play, settings, credits, and close using glossy cyan-cobalt fills, navy contour edges, and restrained gold accent cuts. Icons are front-facing, readable at small sizes, and integrated with the button skin family rather than flat generic symbols.
iconSystem.paletteMode: cobalt-cyan base with warm gold accent

motionSystem.hover: Desktop hover uses a coherent premium response: buttons lift slightly, gloss intensifies, inner gold edge catches light, and shadows deepen. Slider hover gently enlarges the handle; toggle hover slightly brightens the track. Panels themselves remain stable to avoid visual noise.
motionSystem.press: Press feedback is quick and tactile: buttons compress 3 to 4 percent with a short inset shadow change, toggle thumb depresses before switching, and slider handle compresses subtly at drag start. Motion stays controlled and polished rather than bouncy.
motionSystem.entrance: On menu reveal, title plate and action stack fade and rise in with stagger under 220ms total impression, while decorative corners softly fade without travel. Modals fade and scale in from 97 to 100 percent so they feel attached to the UI shell.
motionSystem.release: Release returns controls smoothly to their resting scale with shadow normalization and gloss settling. Closing modals fades them out and slightly scales to 98 percent before hiding.
motionSystem.reducedMotion: When reduced motion is preferred, remove lift and travel; keep only small opacity and brightness changes plus immediate state transitions for toggle and slider.
motionSystem.touchBehavior: Touch devices use Activated and drag interactions only, never synthetic hover. Press feedback occurs on touch-down with a slightly longer visible state so taps feel responsive on mobile.

audioSystem.touchBehavior: No UI sounds on touch because audio was not requested.
audioSystem.fallbackBehavior: If a future implementation adds sounds, unresolved audio must be reported and the interface should remain silent rather than fabricating assets.

responsiveStrategy.desktop: View builds _NexusDesktop containing the centered title plate, central action stack, and hidden modal overlays. Desktop preserves ornamental corners at moderate visibility and uses broader modal widths with left-aligned internal content. Buttons rely on hover plus press states, and the Play button remains the clear visual anchor while Settings and Credits remain primary companion actions.
responsiveStrategy.mobile: View also builds _NexusMobile with the same semantic node names beneath the mobile group. Runtime selects it when min(viewport.X, viewport.Y)<600. Mobile reflows the title plate narrower, keeps the primary stack centered but lower for thumb comfort, enlarges touch targets to 48-56px minimum, reduces decorative intensity, and widens modals relative to screen width. No desktop-only hover behavior is synthesized on touch.
responsiveStrategy.tablet: Tablet uses the mobile runtime group when under the runtime threshold logic only if min dimension is below 600; otherwise desktop group remains appropriate. Plan visual scaling so tablet landscape reads like a roomy desktop composition, while portrait tablet still has sufficient modal width and touch target sizing through constraints and UIScale adjustments.

implementationNotes: Create both _NexusDesktop and _NexusMobile Frame groups at View.build() return, each containing matching semantic nodeName counterparts for all visible components; desktop visible initially.
Use local helper functions inside View for repeated construction of glossy button shells, title plate framing, panel shells, labels, and ornamental image wrappers.
Use a shared ButtonEffects module for all hover/press interactions; do not duplicate ad hoc tween logic per button.
Implement actual controller-backed panel state with one active modal at a time: opening Settings hides Credits, opening Credits hides Settings, close buttons hide only their respective panel.
Play interaction must close the menu root and then fire a clearly named local hook such as OnPlayRequested or equivalent local bindable callback; do not invent remote networking.
Provide nonvisual controller nodes named PanelStateController and OnPlayRequestedHook to make the intended runtime wiring explicit for verification.
Keep main screen free of unrequested systems: no shop, no rewards, no currency, no progression, no tabs beyond requested actions, no inventory, no ranks.
Modal backdrops may dim the hero stack with a semi-transparent navy overlay, but the overlay should be part of modal handling rather than a new navigation system.
For generated artwork, keep labels as live TextLabel/TextButton text layered above image skins; never bake Play, Settings, Credits, Close, or AURORA into images.
Use distinct child artwork pieces for slider track and handle, and for toggle on/off states, under the existing slider and toggle parent controls so the controller can update state cleanly.
Use UIAspectRatioConstraint on ornamental and artwork pieces that must preserve fixed proportions, especially title plate ends, corner details, toggle art, and slider handle.
Use UITextSizeConstraint on all live text-bearing controls to preserve readability across desktop, tablet, and phone portrait widths.

If credits content is not specified beyond having a small panel, keep it concise and generic, such as a short heading and a brief live text block, without inventing extra systems or long scrollable lists.
Panels should start hidden and be opened and closed by the actual controller, not by View-only static visibility assumptions.
Because audio was not requested, the UI must remain silent rather than attaching placeholder sound assets.
The background should be native Roblox UI layering with restrained gradients and bloom-like panels, not a full illustrated splash that overpowers the controls.

changeInstructions: Build a new main menu titled AURORA.
Include only Play, Settings, and Credits as main actions.
Settings must open a panel containing a Music on/off toggle and Volume slider.
Credits must open a small panel.
Both panels must include Close.
Play must close the menu and fire a clearly named local hook for game integration.
Support desktop and mobile.
Use rich glossy cyan/cobalt artwork with thick navy edges, warm gold highlights, ornamental corner details, and a title plate.
Use Gemini-generated matching skins and icons for buttons, panels, slider parts, toggle parts, and action icons.
Keep text live and readable.
Implement coherent hover and press animation.
Use a native background layout with restrained decoration.
Ensure panels open and close in the actual controller.
